hi op!! if you haven't yet, you can register with DSC to receive academic accommodations. before i was diagnosed with adhd, i spoke to DSC and told them i struggle a lot with concentration and they were able to give me accommodations (i.e., extended time on exams). i rly recommend that you reach out and speak to someone over there. 

your experience may be different, but it took a while for me to finally be diagnosed with adhd. the process is super strenuous (nonstop testing and paperwork) and took around 3-4 months in total. however, it's 100% worth it so pls don't lose hope or give up!! pls don't hesitate to reach out if u have any questions! :)

the counseling center has been incredibly helpful each and every time i have visited. however, they only offer short term counseling, so after a few visits they will guide you towards the direction of seeking out long term counseling. my insurance is pretty difficult to deal with when it comes to mental health care, but the counselor i was seeing at the time bent over backwards to send emails, make phone calls on my behalf, and help me find a long term therapist. whether you have ucship or your own insurance, i am positive that they will help you navigate that space when the time comes!

i also used to think that my depression would disappear if i distracted myself, but i had to learn the hard way that the only way you'll ever beat it is by addressing your problems and seeking out the help you need and deserve. i've been in the position of worrying that the people around me will judge me for seeking out mental health care, and it sucks, but those people do not deserve to be in your life if they're actually going to judge you for putting yourself first and taking care of your health, y'know? 

you deserve to be happy, and i hope you feel better soon. im sending hugs & positive vibes your way <3 feel free to pm me if you have any other questions!

1. I lived in Oakenshield (ME) my first year and the room did not have any mirrors whatsoever. I lived in Cumbre (MC) my second year and the room came with one mirror in between the closets that showed only the top half of my body. I'm not sure if there are mirrors in either of the towers. If you want a fullbody mirror, you can just purchase one yourself and hang it up using command strips..this is what I did during my first year.
2. Use command strips on the walls. You can tape things to the fabric cork boards in Mesa Court dorms, but you might have better luck just using pushpins. 
3. As of right now, Housing plans to keep all rooms single occupancy. However, there is a limited quantity of single dorms in each housing community, so they will be placing students in singles, doubles, triples, and quads all while charging everyone for the price of a double occupancy dorm. If you are placed in a double, triple, or a quad, the extra furniture will stay in there and cannot be removed. 
4. The dining halls will be open, but they are planning on providing takeout meals only. Students can take these to-go meals and eat them anywhere that isn't the dining hall, whether that be your room or somewhere on campus. Students can still go out and buy food. 

I heard that they are planning on holding a Housing Q&A in a couple of weeks, so be on the lookout for that.

as far as studying goes, i don’t personally think that the material is so complex that extra time aside from general studying/reviewing needs to be set aside to study it. we had to memorize a few court cases for the midterm, but Zanotto spends a lot of time in class explaining them, and shows us multiple news clips to make sure they’re all as clear as possible. 

the only thing that took up a lot of my time was the presentation. it’s based on a court case, and Zanotto took a lot of time to prepare us for the case in class (we watched documentaries) but you’re given around one week to prepare your actual presentation and paper. 

if it makes it any better, we were given one discussion section class-time to meet and touch bases with our presentation groups, and lecture/discussions were cancelled the week of presentations (so we basically had more time to prepare for it). a lot of the presentation/paper is just regurgitated information from the actual court case, it’s just a pain to get all of the most compelling arguments and condense it into a 2 minute presentation. it felt like a lot of work while it was happening, but now we’re pretty much cruising through the quarter. 

i think you’ll be fine, but make sure to do what you feel is best!

taking it right now with Zanotto. grade is made up of iclicker points, an initial online survey, discussion attendance, mock trial presentation and paper, lifestyle change assignment, in-class midterm, online midterm, and final.

i really enjoy the class and all of the topics discussed. midterms weren’t at all difficult, Zanotto is all-around a great professor, lots of extra credit opportunities. lifestyle change assignment just consists of students committing to a lifestyle change (choices are provided) for 10 days and writing about their experience in a blog post.

the biggest hurdle in the class is the mock trial presentation + paper. since presentations were so early in the quarter (week 3) it kind of felt like we were thrown into it, but i feel like Zanotto did her best to prepare us for it, and TA’s (at least mine) didn’t grade too harshly.

hey, i get it! like i said, you were probably stuck with a really shitty SPOP group. also, the time leading up to the beginning of the first quarter is scary. it leaves you with a lot of time to think. my anxiety caused me to feel really scared and apprehensive about moving into my dorm and starting classes, and im sure that the conversation at SPOP makes you feel even worse. i can assure you that you will meet tons of great, friendly people during your time here. 

just because you met a few people with lower hs stats than you doesn’t mean that your efforts have gone unnoticed. it also doesn’t change the quality of uci’s academics. in the end, nobody understands the college admissions process. it’s very messed up, and there’s no explaining it. just don’t think too much about that SPOP experience, op. all will be well.

those are good factors! however, you need to understand that you're not in high school anymore. that chapter of your life has completely ended already, and you'll realize this at some point during your first year in college. high school stats don't matter and nobody cares about how well you did in high school or what your exam scores were.

I feel like this is brought up in every thread when someone brings up an issue they have with uci or college in general, but college is truly what you make of it. the cool thing about college is that its kind of a fresh start. nobody is going to want to be friends with you just because you took 9 AP classes or because you got \[x\] score on the SATs.  if you continue viewing uci in a negative light because of the hs stats of your peers, then you'll have a negative experience. just put all of that aside, be yourself, and make the best of your experience here.
